subject: math
title: Numbers to 10 000: Place Value, Comparing and Number Lines
seo_title: Grade 4 Numbers to 10 000 Math Worksheets: Free, with Answer Key (Ontario)
standard_text: Read, represent, compose, and decompose whole numbers up to and including 10 000, using appropriate tools and strategies, and describe various ways they are used in everyday life
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 math worksheets on numbers to 10 000 for the Ontario curriculum: base ten blocks, the value of each digit, expanded form, comparing and ordering, and number lines. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: The place of a digit tells you its value. The 5 in 4053 is worth 50.
key_sub: Write 0 for an empty place: four thousand fifty-three is 4053, not 453 or 40 053. To compare, count the digits first, then compare from the left.
body_html:
Thousands, hundreds, tens and ones

A 4-digit number has four places: thousands, hundreds, tens and ones. 10 ones make 1 ten. 10 tens make 1 hundred. 10 hundreds make 1 thousand. 10 thousands make 10 000.

The value of a digit

The place tells you what a digit is worth.

If a place is empty, write 0 there. The 0 keeps the other digits in the right places.

Write the number

Write “four thousand fifty-three” as a number.

4 thousands, 0 hundreds, 5 tens, 3 ones. Write 4, 0, 5, 3.

Answer: 4053 (not 453 or 40 053)

Expanded form and decomposing

Expanded form shows the value of each digit: 4361 = 4000 + 300 + 60 + 1. You can also decompose a number another way. Trade 1 hundred for 10 tens.

Decompose

Decompose 4361 in two ways.

4 thousands, 3 hundreds, 6 tens and 1 one. Or 4 thousands, 2 hundreds, 16 tens and 1 one.

Answer: 4000 + 300 + 60 + 1 = 4000 + 200 + 160 + 1

Compare and order

First count the digits: a 5-digit number is greater than a 4-digit number. If both have 4 digits, compare the thousands, then the hundreds, then the tens, then the ones.

Compare

5602 ☐ 5620

Thousands: 5 = 5. Hundreds: 6 = 6. Tens: 0 tens < 2 tens.

Answer: 5602 < 5620

> means “is greater than”. < means “is less than”. The open side faces the greater number.

Number lines

Before you read a number line, work out the size of each jump. Count the jumps between two labelled numbers.

Numbers in everyday life

We use numbers to 10 000 to count seats in a hockey arena, books in a library, kilometres on a road trip and dollars raised for the Terry Fox Run. Read the number first, then think about what each digit means.

NumberWhere you might see itIn words
6248seats in a hockey arenasix thousand two hundred forty-eight
2085kilometres on a road triptwo thousand eighty-five
$2700money raised for a charity runtwo thousand seven hundred dollars

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Leaving out the zero (four thousand fifty-three = 453)Write 0 for the empty hundreds place: 4053
Writing an extra zero (4053 = 40 053)A number in the thousands has 4 digits
Reading the digit, not its value (the 5 in 4053 is 5)The 5 is in the tens place: 50
Writing 14 hundreds inside the number (3 thousands, 14 hundreds = 31 400)14 hundreds = 1400, so 3000 + 1400 = 4400
Comparing the first digits only (9989 > 10 000)Count the digits first: 10 000 > 9989
Thinking every mark on a number line is 1, 10 or 100Work out the jump first: 0 to 5000 in 10 jumps means 500 each

faq.q: What number skills are in the Grade 4 Ontario math curriculum?
faq.a: Grade 4 students read, represent, compose and decompose whole numbers up to and including 10 000 (B1.1) and compare and order them (B1.2). They also describe how these numbers are used in everyday life.

faq.q: How do you write 10 000 in Canada?
faq.a: Ontario math resources write 4-digit numbers with no space (4053) and put a space between groups of three digits from 5 digits on (10 000). Commas are not used.

faq.q: How can I help my child with place value to 10 000 at home?
faq.a: Point out big numbers in daily life, such as arena seats, kilometres on a trip or prices, and ask what each digit is worth. Ask your child to say the number in two ways, for example 4361 as 43 hundreds and 61 ones.
No. In Ontario, the EQAO math assessment is written in Grade 3 and Grade 6. Grade 4 place value builds on Grade 3 and prepares students for Grade 6.

sets.title: Base ten blocks: thousands, hundreds, tens and ones

items.e: A big cube is 1000, a flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 3 thousands, 4 hundreds, 2 tens and 6 ones make 3426. Start with the big cubes, then the flats, rods and small cubes.

A big cube is 1000, a flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 2 thousands, 5 hundreds, 0 tens and 7 ones make 2507. There are no tens, so write 0 in that place. Start with the big cubes, then the flats, rods and small cubes.

A big cube is 1000, a flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 4 thousands, 0 hundreds, 3 tens and 8 ones make 4038. There are no hundreds, so write 0 in that place. Start with the big cubes, then the flats, rods and small cubes.
Each rod is 1 ten. There are 2 rods, so there are 2 tens. The number is 3524.
Each flat is 1 hundred. There are 6 flats, so there are 6 hundreds. The number is 2603.

A big cube is 1000, a flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 1 thousand, 2 hundreds, 7 tens and 0 ones make 1270. There are no ones, so write 0 in that place. Start with the big cubes, then the flats, rods and small cubes.

A big cube is 1000, a flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 5 thousands, 0 hundreds, 6 tens and 1 one make 5061. There are no hundreds, so write 0 in that place. Start with the big cubes, then the flats, rods and small cubes.
Count each kind of block: 3 thousands, 6 hundreds, 2 tens and 5 ones. The number is 3625.

items.q: Write “four thousand fifty-three” as a number.
items.e: 4 thousands, 0 hundreds, 5 tens and 3 ones. There are no hundreds, so write 0 there: 4053. It has 4 digits, not 3 (453) or 5 (40 053).
A big cube is 1000, a flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 2 thousands, 4 hundreds, 1 ten and 8 ones make 2418. Start with the big cubes, then the flats, rods and small cubes.
Each big cube is 1 thousand. There are 4 big cubes, so there are 4 thousands. Their value is 4000, but the question asks how many. The number is 4261.

items.q: Which number has 5 thousands, 0 hundreds, 7 tens and 1 one?
items.e: Write the digits in order: thousands 5, hundreds 0, tens 7, ones 1. That is 5071.

A big cube is 1000, a flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 4 thousands, 1 hundred, 0 tens and 0 ones make 4100. There are no tens or ones, so write 0 in those places. Start with the big cubes, then the flats, rods and small cubes.

A big cube is 1000, a flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 3 thousands, 0 hundreds, 0 tens and 9 ones make 3009. There are no hundreds or tens, so write 0 in those places. Start with the big cubes, then the flats, rods and small cubes.
Count each kind of block: 2 thousands, 1 hundred, 5 tens and 4 ones. The number is 2154.

items.q: Write “six thousand nine hundred four” as a number.
items.e: 6 thousands, 9 hundreds, 0 tens and 4 ones: 6904. The 4 is ones, so it goes last. Write 0 for the empty tens place.
Each flat is 100. Count by 100s: 100, 200, 300 … 1000. 10 hundreds make 1 thousand, the same as 1 big cube.
The blocks show 3962. Add 1 flat: now there are 10 flats. Trade 10 flats for 1 big cube. That is 4 thousands, 0 hundreds, 6 tens and 2 ones: 4062.
The blocks show 2793. Add 1 rod: now there are 10 rods. Trade 10 rods for 1 flat. That is 2 thousands, 8 hundreds, 0 tens and 3 ones: 2803.

items.q: Each big cube is 1000. What number do 10 big cubes make?
items.e: Count by 1000s: 1000, 2000, 3000 … 10 000. 10 thousands make 10 000. Ten thousand has 5 digits: 1 and four zeros.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 5 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 5 thousands = 5000. The digit is 5, but its value is 5000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 6 is in the tens place, so it is worth 6 tens = 60. The digit is 6, but its value is 60.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 9 in 4916?
items.e: The 9 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 9 hundreds = 900. The digit is 9, but its value is 900.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 8 in 8305?
items.e: The 8 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 8 thousands = 8000. The digit is 8, but its value is 8000.

items.q: In 6492, which digit is in the hundreds place?
items.e: 6492 has 6 thousands, 4 hundreds, 9 tens and 2 ones. The hundreds digit is 4.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 4 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 4 hundreds = 400. The digit is 4, but its value is 400.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 7 in 1672?
items.e: The 7 is in the tens place, so it is worth 7 tens = 70. The digit is 7, but its value is 70.

items.q: Which number has a 5 in the hundreds place?
items.e: In 4538 the 5 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 500.

items.q: In 9083, which digit is in the thousands place?
items.e: 9083 has 9 thousands, 0 hundreds, 8 tens and 3 ones. The thousands digit is 9.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 5 in 3058?
items.e: The 5 is in the tens place, so it is worth 5 tens = 50. The digit is 5, but its value is 50.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 5 is in the tens place, so it is worth 5 tens = 50. The digit is 5, but its value is 50.

items.q: Which number has an 8 in the tens place?
items.e: In 2781 the 8 is in the tens place, so it is worth 80.

items.q: What number is 1000 more than 5062?
items.e: 1000 more changes only the thousands digit: 5 thousands → 6 thousands. 5062 + 1000 = 6062.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 4 in 7493?
items.e: The 4 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 4 hundreds = 400. The digit is 4, but its value is 400.

items.q: In 3715, which digit is in the tens place?
items.e: 3715 has 3 thousands, 7 hundreds, 1 ten and 5 ones. The tens digit is 1.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 2 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 2 hundreds = 200. The digit is 2, but its value is 200.

items.q: Which number has a 3 in the thousands place?
items.e: In 3740 the 3 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 3000.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 2 in 2741?
items.e: The 2 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 2 thousands = 2000. The digit is 2, but its value is 2000.

items.q: What number is 100 less than 8034?
items.e: There are 0 hundreds, so trade 1 thousand for 10 hundreds: 7 thousands, 10 hundreds. Take away 1 hundred: 7 thousands, 9 hundreds, 3 tens, 4 ones = 7934.

items.q: What number is 10 more than 6995?
items.e: 6995 has 9 tens. 10 more makes 10 tens, which is 1 hundred. That makes 10 hundreds, which is 1 thousand. 6995 + 10 = 7005.

sets.title: Expanded form and decomposing in different ways

items.q: What is 5062 in expanded form?
items.e: 5062 is 5 thousands, 0 hundreds, 6 tens and 2 ones. Write the value of each digit and skip the zeros: 5062 = 5000 + 60 + 2.

items.q: What is 8401 in expanded form?
items.e: 8401 is 8 thousands, 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 1 one. Write the value of each digit and skip the zeros: 8401 = 8000 + 400 + 1.

items.q: What number is 5000 + 200 + 9?
items.e: 5000 + 200 + 9 = 5209. That is 5 thousands, 2 hundreds, 0 tens and 9 ones. Write 0 for each empty place, so the number has 4 digits.

items.q: What number is 7000 + 30 + 4?
items.e: 7000 + 30 + 4 = 7034. That is 7 thousands, 0 hundreds, 3 tens and 4 ones. Write 0 for each empty place, so the number has 4 digits.

items.q: What is 2970 in expanded form?
items.e: 2970 is 2 thousands, 9 hundreds, 7 tens and 0 ones. Write the value of each digit and skip the zeros: 2970 = 2000 + 900 + 70.

items.q: What number is 3000 + 800 + 6?
items.e: 3000 + 800 + 6 = 3806. That is 3 thousands, 8 hundreds, 0 tens and 6 ones. Write 0 for each empty place, so the number has 4 digits.

items.q: 47 hundreds is the same as what number?
items.e: 1 hundred = 100, so 47 hundreds = 47 × 100 = 4700. That is 4 thousands and 7 hundreds.

items.q: What is 6038 in expanded form?
items.e: 6038 is 6 thousands, 0 hundreds, 3 tens and 8 ones. Write the value of each digit and skip the zeros: 6038 = 6000 + 30 + 8.

items.q: What number is 9000 + 5?
items.e: 9000 + 5 = 9005. That is 9 thousands, 0 hundreds, 0 tens and 5 ones. Write 0 for each empty place, so the number has 4 digits.

items.q: 4361 = 4 thousands, 2 hundreds, ☐ tens and 1 one. What number goes in the box?
items.e: Only 2 hundreds are used, so 1 hundred becomes 10 tens. 10 + 6 = 16 tens. Check: 4000 + 200 + 160 + 1 = 4361.

items.q: How many hundreds are in 3600?
items.e: 3 thousands = 30 hundreds. 30 + 6 = 36 hundreds. Check: 36 × 100 = 3600. (6 is only the hundreds digit.)

items.q: What is 4527 in expanded form?
items.e: 4527 is 4 thousands, 5 hundreds, 2 tens and 7 ones. Write the value of each digit and skip the zeros: 4527 = 4000 + 500 + 20 + 7.

items.q: What number is 400 + 6000 + 70 + 2?
items.e: 400 + 6000 + 70 + 2 = 6472. That is 6 thousands, 4 hundreds, 7 tens and 2 ones. The parts are not in order, so put each digit in its own place.

items.q: 3728 = 2 thousands, ☐ hundreds, 2 tens and 8 ones. What number goes in the box?
items.e: Only 2 thousands are used, so 1 thousand becomes 10 hundreds. 10 + 7 = 17 hundreds. Check: 2000 + 1700 + 20 + 8 = 3728.

items.q: How many tens are in 2480?
What number is 3 thousands, 14 hundreds and 5 tens?
items.e: 14 hundreds = 1400. 3000 + 1400 + 50 = 4450. Do not write 14 inside the number.

items.q: Which is another way to make 5380?
items.e: Trade 1 thousand for 10 hundreds: 4000 + 1300 + 80 = 5380. (The others make 6380, 4480 and 6100.)

items.q: What number is 5 thousands, 11 hundreds and 9 ones?
items.e: 11 hundreds = 1100 = 1 thousand and 1 hundred. 5000 + 1100 + 9 = 6109.

items.q: Which is the same as 6407?
items.e: 6 thousands = 60 hundreds, so 6407 has 60 + 4 = 64 hundreds and 7 ones. 6400 + 7 = 6407.

items.q: What number is 2 thousands, 6 hundreds, 13 tens and 4 ones?
Which number is the greatest?
items.e: All four numbers have the same number of digits. Compare from the left. 6702 and 6270 are the closest: they first differ in the hundreds place, 7 > 2. So 6702 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: All four numbers have the same number of digits. Compare from the left. 8019 and 8091 are the closest: they first differ in the tens place, 1 < 9. So 8019 is the least.

items.q: Which number is greater than 6380?
items.e: Same thousands. Hundreds: 6803 has 8 hundreds and 6380 has 3 hundreds. So 6803 > 6380. The others are all less than 6380.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 5602 and 5620 have the same thousands and hundreds. Tens: 0 tens < 2 tens, so 5602 < 5620. The others are false: 3070 < 3700, 9999 < 10 000 and 8143 > 8134.

items.q: Which number is between 6200 and 6300?
items.e: A number between 6200 and 6300 has 6 thousands and 2 hundreds. 6248 fits. 6320 is too big, 6028 is too small and 2648 is too small.

items.q: Put 5620, 5062 and 5206 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: All have 5 thousands. Hundreds: 0 < 2 < 6. Order: 5062, 5206, 5620.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: 10 000 has 5 digits. All the others have 4 digits or fewer, so 10 000 is the greatest, even though 9989 starts with a 9.

items.q: Use the digits 6, 0, 3 and 8 once each. What is the greatest number you can make?
items.e: Put the biggest digit in the thousands place, then the next biggest: 8, 6, 3, 0. That is 8630.

items.q: Which number is less than 8000?
items.e: 7999 has only 7 thousands. The others have 8 thousands and more, so they are greater than 8000.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 6999 has 6 thousands and 7000 has 7 thousands, so 6999 < 7000. The others are false: 4200 > 4020, 999 < 1000 and 3850 > 3805.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: 423 has only 3 digits. The others have 4 digits, so they are all greater. 423 is the least.

items.q: Put 8710, 10 000, 8170 and 8701 in order from greatest to least.
items.e: 10 000 has 5 digits, so it is the greatest. 8170 has the fewest hundreds. 8710 > 8701 because 1 ten > 0 tens. Order: 10 000, 8710, 8701, 8170.

items.q: Which number is between 4900 and 5000?
items.e: A number between 4900 and 5000 has 4 thousands and 9 hundreds. 4960 fits. 5960 and 5004 are more than 5000, and 4096 is less than 4900.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: All four numbers have the same number of digits. Compare from the left. 5505 and 5500 are the closest: they first differ in the ones place, 5 > 0. So 5505 is the greatest.

items.q: Use the digits 7, 0, 4 and 1 once each. What is the least 4-digit number you can make?
items.e: A 4-digit number cannot start with 0. Put the smallest other digit first: 1. Then 0, 4, 7: 1047. (0147 is just 147, which has only 3 digits.)

items.q: Put 3805, 3085, 3580 and 3508 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: All have 3 thousands. Hundreds: 0 < 5 < 8, so 3085 is the least and 3805 is the greatest. 3508 < 3580 because 0 tens < 8 tens. Order: 3085, 3508, 3580, 3805.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Same thousands. Hundreds: 5 hundreds > 0 hundreds, so 8500 > 8050. The others are false: 2360 < 2630, 6040 > 640 and 1007 < 1070.

items.q: Which number is greater than 9980?
items.e: 10 000 is 20 more than 9980. 9908 and 9089 have fewer tens or hundreds, and 998 has only 3 digits.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: All four numbers have the same number of digits. Compare from the left. 7546 and 7564 are the closest: they first differ in the tens place, 4 < 6. So 7546 is the least.

items.q: Put 7340, 734, 7034 and 7403 in order from greatest to least.
items.e: 734 has only 3 digits, so it is the least. The others have 7 thousands. Hundreds: 4 > 3 > 0. Order: 7403, 7340, 7034, 734.

sets.title: Number lines and numbers in everyday life

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 10 000 there are 10 jumps, so each mark is 1000. The arrow is 3 marks after 0: 1000, 2000, 3000.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 6000 to 7000 there are 10 jumps, so each mark is 100. The arrow is 3 marks after 6500: 6600, 6700, 6800. (6080 counts each mark as 10.)

items.q: Count on by 1000s: 2350, 3350, 4350, ☐. What number comes next?
items.e: Counting by 1000s changes only the thousands digit: 2, 3, 4, then 5. The next number is 5350.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 2400 to 2500 there are 10 jumps, so each mark is 10. The arrow is 3 marks after 2400: 2410, 2420, 2430.

items.q: Is 7820 closer to 7000 or to 8000?
items.e: Halfway between 7000 and 8000 is 7500. 7820 is after 7500, so it is closer to 8000. (7820 has 7 thousands, but it is only 180 away from 8000.)

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 5000 there are 10 marks, so each mark is 500. The arrow is 5 marks after 0: 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500. (5000 counts each mark as 1000.)

items.q: Count back by 100s: 6230, 6130, 6030, ☐. What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 100 less. 6030 has 0 hundreds, so trade 1 thousand for 10 hundreds: 6030 − 100 = 5930.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: Each mark is 100. The arrow is 1 mark before 10 000, so it points to 10 000 − 100 = 9900.

items.q: Is 2340 closer to 2300 or to 2400?
items.e: Halfway between 2300 and 2400 is 2350. 2340 is before 2350, so it is closer to 2300: it is 40 away from 2300 and 60 away from 2400.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 3000 to 4000 there are 5 jumps, so each mark is 200. The arrow is 3 marks after 4000: 4200, 4400, 4600. (4300 counts each mark as 100.)

items.q: A hockey arena in Kingston has 6248 seats. What is the value of the 2 in 6248?
items.e: The 2 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 2 hundreds = 200.

items.q: A school library in Ottawa has four thousand six hundred eight books. Which number is that?
items.e: 4 thousands, 6 hundreds, 0 tens and 8 ones: 4608. Write 0 for the empty tens place.

items.q: Volunteers counted 1209 loons on lakes in Muskoka. How do you write 1209 in words?
items.e: 1209 is 1 thousand, 2 hundreds, 0 tens and 9 ones: one thousand two hundred nine. The 9 is in the ones place, so it is nine, not ninety.

items.q: A sugar bush made 3460 L of maple syrup this spring. Which shows 3460 in expanded form?
items.e: 3460 is 3 thousands, 4 hundreds, 6 tens and 0 ones: 3000 + 400 + 60. The 6 is in the tens place, so it is worth 60.

items.q: Students at a school in Hamilton raised $2700 for the Terry Fox Run. The money is all in $100 bills. How many $100 bills is that?
items.e: 2700 = 27 hundreds, because 27 × 100 = 2700. So there are 27 bills of $100. (7 is only the hundreds digit.)

items.q: Nathan's family drove 2085 km on a summer road trip. Mei's family drove 2058 km. Who drove farther?
items.e: Both numbers have 2 thousands and 0 hundreds. Tens: 8 tens > 5 tens, so 2085 > 2058. The numbers use the same digits, but the places are different.

items.q: A school in Mississauga bought 3 boxes of 1000 stickers, 6 packs of 10 stickers and 4 single stickers. How many stickers is that?
items.e: 3 thousands, 0 hundreds, 6 tens and 4 ones: 3000 + 60 + 4 = 3064. There are no hundreds, so write 0 in the hundreds place.

items.q: Four schools collected cans for a food drive: Maple School 1305, Pine School 1530, Birch School 1350 and Cedar School 1053. Which school collected the most cans?
items.e: All four numbers have 1 thousand. Compare the hundreds: 1530 has 5 hundreds, 1350 and 1305 have 3, and 1053 has 0. So 1530 is the greatest. Pine School collected the most.

items.q: Ethan's town had a Canada Day fireworks show. More than 4500 people came, but fewer than 4600. Which number could be how many people came?
items.e: The number must be between 4500 and 4600, so it has 4 thousands and 5 hundreds. 4562 fits. 4652 and 5462 are too big, and 4056 is too small.

items.q: A ski hill sold 9995 lift tickets this winter. On the last day it sold 5 more. How many lift tickets did it sell in all?
items.e: 9995 + 5 = 10 000. 10 ones make 1 ten, 10 tens make 1 hundred, 10 hundreds make 1 thousand and 10 thousands make 10 000. The answer has 5 digits.
